questions.solution: 10 northings and 26 eastings (as printed). Distance between consecutive northing and easting lines is 2 cm on the map; as per the scale 2 cm = 1 km, each grid square = 1 km2. Therefore (10 x 25) sq. km = 250 sq. km. (Printed working says 26 eastings but multiplies by 25; the official final answer is 250 km2.)

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the river Krishna.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). River Krishna: rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats (Maharashtra), flows east/south-east through Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh (past Vijayawada) and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Draw the line and label 'Krishna'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Eastern Ghats.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Eastern Ghats: a broken chain of hills parallel to the east coast, from Odisha (south of the Mahanadi) through Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu, meeting the Western Ghats at the Nilgiris. Mark a broken band just inland of the east coast and label 'Eastern Ghats'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

concepts: population density distribution in South India
questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label a densely populated area in the Southern part of India.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Densely populated area in southern India: the Kerala (Malabar) coast, or the Tamil Nadu coast / Cauvery delta, or the Andhra delta region. Shade one such area (for example coastal Kerala) and label it.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Konkan coastal plain.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Konkan coastal plain: the narrow coastal strip on the west coast between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, from about Daman in the north to Goa in the south (Maharashtra and Goa). Shade the strip and label 'Konkan coast'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark with an arrow and label the direction of Western disturbance.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Western Disturbance: an arrow coming from the west (Mediterranean / Iran) over Pakistan and entering north-west India (Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir), pointing east-south-east. Draw the arrow and label 'Western Disturbance'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Thar Desert.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Thar Desert: western Rajasthan, west of the Aravalli range and running into Pakistan (Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Barmer). Shade it and label 'Thar Desert'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Andaman Sea.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Andaman Sea: the sea east of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, between the islands and Myanmar/Thailand, in the eastern Bay of Bengal. Shade the water east of the Andaman islands and label 'Andaman Sea'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the city Chennai.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Chennai: east (Coromandel) coast of Tamil Nadu on the Bay of Bengal, about 13 deg N, 80.3 deg E. Mark a dot on the coast and label 'Chennai'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and name the highest peak of Himalayas in India.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Highest peak of the Himalayas in India: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), on the Sikkim-Nepal border, about 27.7 deg N, 88.1 deg E. Mark it in the north-east, north of West Bengal, and label 'Kanchenjunga'. (Nanda Devi, 7,816 m, is the highest peak lying entirely within India; the board answer for this question is Kanchenjunga.)

questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Mark it in the sea off Mumbai and label 'Mumbai High'.

questions.question: What causes snowfall in Kashmir during winter?
questions.solution: (d) Temperate cyclone. Western disturbances from the Mediterranean bring snowfall in Kashmir and rainfall in North-west India.

questions.question: Which of the following helps in soil conservation?
questions.solution: (a) Afforestation. Planting trees protects the soil from erosion.

questions.question: Which means of irrigation can be developed with minimum expenditure?
questions.solution: (d) Drip irrigation, as given in the printed key (it is described as the simplest and cheapest to operate because it saves water). Note: well irrigation is also very cheap to develop, so this question is debatable.

Read the table and identify the pair that is correctly matched:
Natural Vegetation Belt | Tree
P. Tropical evergreen | Babool
Q. Tropical deciduous | Teak
R. Littoral | Ebony
S. Mountain forest | Banyan
questions.solution: (b) Q. Tropical deciduous forests have Sal, Teak, Arjun, Mahua, Shisham, Palas, Mulberry, Semul and Sandalwood.

questions.question: Bauxite is the ore of:
questions.solution: (a) Aluminium

questions.question: Identify the source of energy that leads to pollution:
questions.solution: (c) Natural gas, a non-renewable fossil fuel that creates pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a centre for the iron and steel industry?
questions.solution: (b) Bengaluru (hub of the IT industry).

questions.question: Which of the following farming method is used to grow tea on a large scale?
questions.solution: (b) Plantation farming. Tea is a commercial crop grown on large estates by plantation farming. (The printed key shows (a) Subsistence, which contradicts its own explanation.)

questions.question: Which of the following means of transport has best use during floods/earthquake?
questions.solution: (a) Airways. Floods and earthquakes disrupt waterways and land transport.

questions.question: Which of the following is a biodegradable waste?
questions.solution: (b) Waste paper. Broken glass, polythene and plastic bags are non-biodegradable.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: 'Himalayas act as a climatic divide'. Justify the statement giving two reasons.
questions.solution: 1. The Himalayas prevent the cold winds of Central Asia from entering India, so India does not experience severe cold winters. 2. They stop the rain-bearing monsoon winds from leaving the country, so India receives sufficient rainfall.

marking_points.point: Prevent cold Central Asian winds from entering India, avoiding severe winters
Block the monsoon winds from leaving, causing sufficient rainfall in India

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Differentiate between Southwest Monsoon and Retreating Monsoon. (Any two differences)
questions.solution: Southwest monsoon: blows from the south-west; blows from sea to land; causes rainfall in July-September; rain in western part, south-western, Gangetic plain and north-eastern parts. Retreating monsoon: blows from the north-east; blows from land to sea; rainfall in October-November; rain in south-eastern parts of India. (Any two)

marking_points.point: First valid difference (direction / sea-land / season / region)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
concepts: distance from sea and monsoon rainfall
questions.question: Give a geographical reason for the following: Kolkata gets more rain than Delhi during rainy season.
questions.solution: Kolkata is situated in the Ganga delta region near the Bay of Bengal, whereas Delhi is located inland in the middle course of the Ganga. The Bay of Bengal branch of the SW Monsoon is exhausted as it blows up the Ganga plain, so Kolkata receives more rainfall.

marking_points.point: Kolkata is near the Bay of Bengal / in the delta while Delhi is far inland; monsoon branch loses moisture on the way

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a geographical reason for the following: Though both are hill stations, Shimla experiences snowfall during the winters but Ooty does not.
questions.solution: Ooty lies south of the Tropic of Cancer in the tropical zone, whereas Shimla lies in the temperate zone at higher latitude; hence Shimla gets snowfall but Ooty does not.

marking_points.point: Shimla is at a higher latitude (temperate zone) while Ooty is in the tropical zone

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
concepts: northeast monsoon is dry land wind
questions.question: Give a geographical reason for the following: Winter monsoons bring less rain.
questions.solution: The winter monsoon winds are dry as they blow from land to sea; hence they cause less rainfall.

marking_points.point: They blow from land to sea so are dry

questions.question:
Study the climate data of Station X and answer the questions that follow:
Month: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec

Rainfall (cm): 1.5 0.9 0.5 - - 12.5 17.8 18.5 12.5 12.5 6.2 2.1
Calculate the annual range of temperature of Station X.
questions.solution: Annual range = highest (July 41.0 C) - lowest (January 8.4 C) = 32.6 C.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question:
Study the climate data of Station X and answer the questions that follow:
Month: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
Temp (C): 8.4 11.5 21.6 28.3 35.1 38.5 41.0 38.0 30.8 29.2 15.6 10.2
Rainfall (cm): 1.5 0.9 0.5 - - 12.5 17.8 18.5 12.5 12.5 6.2 2.1
Is the Station X located in coastal area or in the continental interior?
questions.solution: Continental interior, as the temperature is high with a large annual range and rainfall is received mainly in the monsoon months such as August.

marking_points.point: Continental interior, with reason (high temperature range / rainfall concentrated in the monsoon)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is Black soil found suitable for the production of cotton? (Any two points)
questions.solution: It is fine textured and clayey; moisture retentive (sticky when wet, cracks when dry); rich in lime, magnesium and iron; poor in phosphorus, nitrogen and organic matter. (Any two)

marking_points.point: Second valid point (e.g. moisture retentive / rich in lime, magnesium, iron)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one difference between each of the following: Alluvial soil of Uttarakhand and alluvial soil of West Bengal.
questions.solution: Alluvial soil of Uttarakhand is coarser in texture; in West Bengal it is finer in texture.

marking_points.point: Uttarakhand alluvium coarser / West Bengal alluvium finer in texture

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one difference between each of the following: Transported soil and residual soil.
questions.solution: Transported soil is moved away from the place where it was formed (ex-situ), while residual soil remains at the place where it is formed (in-situ).

marking_points.point: Transported soil moved from place of formation vs residual soil remains in situ

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to Laterite soil, answer the questions that follow: How is Laterite soil formed?
questions.solution: Laterite soil is formed in high temperature and intense rainfall with alternate wet and dry periods, leading to leaching of the soil.

marking_points.point: High temperature and heavy rainfall with alternate wet and dry periods causing leaching

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to Laterite soil, answer the questions that follow: How can Laterite soil be made productive?
questions.solution: By substantial use of manure and fertilizers.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to Laterite soil, answer the questions that follow: Name one region where Laterite soil is found.

answer_items.prompt: Region where laterite soil is found

questions.solution: Eastern Ghats or Western Ghats.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention two causes of soil erosion in India.
questions.solution: Deforestation and overgrazing.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention a soil conservation method suitable for hilly area.
questions.solution: Terrace farming or contour ploughing (any one).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: How is tropical monsoon forest useful for the Indian economy? (Any two points)
questions.solution: Tropical monsoon forest is used for lumbering and produces timber for buildings, railway tracks, furniture etc.

marking_points.point: Timber used for buildings, railway tracks, furniture etc. (or another valid economic use)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention the climatic condition that leads to the development of tropical desert vegetation.
questions.solution: Tropical desert vegetation is found in areas getting less than 25 cm rainfall with an average temperature of 25 C to 27 C.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Mountains have varied vegetation.
questions.solution: Mountain vegetation differs with altitude. As height increases, temperature decreases; trees at higher altitude are conical (coniferous forests) while lower elevations have broad-leaved forests.

marking_points.point: Temperature falls with altitude so vegetation varies with height

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Stilt like/aerial roots are a typical feature of littoral forest.
questions.solution: The roots provide structural support in marshy soil and supply oxygen for respiration during high tides.

marking_points.point: Support in soft/marshy soil, and/or oxygen for respiration during high tides

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: The tropical evergreen forests do not look bare at any time of the year.
questions.solution: They do not experience any dry season, so trees do not shed all their leaves at one time.

marking_points.point: No dry season, trees shed leaves at different times so are always green

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: How has the rising population of India resulted in the loss of forest cover? (Any one point)
questions.solution: Rising population increases demand for land for cultivation and shelter; shifting cultivation and deforestation to meet this demand deplete the forest cover.

marking_points.point: Growing demand for land (cultivation, shelter) leads to deforestation

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention any two forest conservation methods that may be adopted to protect the forests.
questions.solution: Afforestation, reforestation, community engagement (any two).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention one advantage and one disadvantage of using tank irrigation.
questions.solution: Advantage: tanks are cheap and widely used. Disadvantage: tanks become dry in summer; siltation can take place.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: What is the advantage of using Drip irrigation?
questions.solution: Efficient water conservation method, cost friendly, helpful in arid climates (any one).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is Drip irrigation not practiced on a large scale in India?
questions.solution: Initial cost is expensive and the system is vulnerable to silting and clogging.

marking_points.point: High initial cost / clogging and silting

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Sprinkler irrigation is gaining popularity in recent times.
questions.solution: Water is used efficiently and less wastage takes place.

marking_points.point: Efficient use of water with less wastage

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Tube well irrigation is used in Punjab.
questions.solution: Punjab depends on groundwater; tube wells irrigate large areas in comparatively less time and can irrigate throughout the year.

marking_points.point: Punjab depends on groundwater / tube wells irrigate large areas quickly and all year

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason to explain each of the following: North India has more area under canal irrigation.
questions.solution: The soil of Northern India is permeable/level plains and perennial rivers with high groundwater level favour canal development.

marking_points.point: Level plains / soft soil / perennial rivers favour canal construction

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to the picture below, answer the questions that follow: Name the water conservation practice shown in the above picture.
questions.solution: Rainwater harvesting.

questions.question: With reference to the picture below, answer the questions that follow: How does this system help to reduce floods?
questions.solution: Water harvesting increases soil moisture and stores excess water, which reduces runoff and the risk of flooding.

marking_points.point: Stores excess water / reduces runoff and so reduces flood risk

questions.figure_desc: Picture of a water conservation practice (rainwater harvesting system) not reproduced

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to the picture below, answer the questions that follow: Why is water conservation necessary? (Any two reasons)
questions.solution: Groundwater level is falling with climate change, so conserve water to raise it; population is increasing while water sources decrease, so water must be saved for scarcity and future generations. (Any two)

marking_points.point: Rising population / scarcity, save for future generations (any second valid reason)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Name any three varieties of coal produced in India.
questions.solution: Bituminous, lignite and peat (anthracite is also a variety).

marking_points.point: Any three correct varieties of coal

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Name the variety of coal widely used in iron and Steel Industries of India.

answer_items.prompt: Coal variety used in iron and steel industry

questions.solution: Bituminous coal.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Name the state that is the largest producer of iron ore in India.
questions.solution: Printed key: Chhattisgarh. (Odisha is generally cited as the largest producer; accept either Odisha or Chhattisgarh.)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention two ways in which Hirakud dam has helped the people of Odisha.
questions.solution: It controls and mitigates floods in the Mahanadi river basin and provides water for agriculture, enhancing irrigation facilities. (Hydroelectric power generation is also acceptable.)

marking_points.point: Irrigation / water supply for agriculture (or power generation)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Across which river is the Hirakud dam built?

answer_items.prompt: River on which Hirakud dam is built

questions.solution: Mahanadi.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give reasons for each of the following: Geothermal energy is not popular in India.
questions.solution: India has limited geothermal resources compared to other countries.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give reasons for each of the following: Solar energy is gaining popularity.
questions.solution: Solar energy is renewable, produces minimal greenhouse gases and its production cost is low.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give reasons for each of the following: Petroleum is considered a harmful source of energy.
questions.solution: Petroleum is a fossil fuel which, when burned, emits harmful greenhouse gases causing ozone depletion and global warming.

marking_points.point: Burning fossil fuel emits greenhouse gases causing pollution/global warming

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is agriculture considered an important sector of Indian economy? (Any two points)
questions.solution: It feeds millions of people; raises livestock and provides fodder (over 60% of land arable, about 70% of rural families depend on it); creates employment (about 58.4% of the workforce); supplies raw materials to industries like cotton and jute textiles, sugar, vanaspati, food processing; supports small scale and cottage industries. (Any two)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: What is mixed farming?
questions.solution: Mixed farming is a type of farming in which a farmer carries out different agricultural practices (crop growing) on a single farm and rears cattle simultaneously, to increase income from different sources.

marking_points.point: Crop cultivation along with rearing of livestock on the same farm

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention any one advantage of mixed farming.
questions.solution: Maintains soil fertility, soil biodiversity, minimises soil erosion and helps conserve water (any one).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain each of the following: West Bengal is a leading producer of jute.
questions.solution: West Bengal has hot and humid climate, sufficient rainfall and irrigation facilities favourable for jute.

marking_points.point: Hot humid climate / sufficient rainfall / alluvial soil, irrigation

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Millets are fast becoming the popular food crops.
questions.solution: Millets have diverse health benefits; low in calories and rich in fibre.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain each of the following: More than two ratoon crops are not advisable for sugarcane farmers.
questions.solution: With each successive ratoon crop the yield of sugarcane declines.

marking_points.point: Yield declines with successive ratoon crops

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to tea cultivation, explain the term 'fine pluck'.
questions.solution: Fine plucking is the method of plucking only shoots with two leaves and a bud.

marking_points.point: Plucking only two leaves and a bud

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Name the Indian state that leads in coffee production.
questions.solution: Karnataka.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is cotton grown as a Kharif crop in India?
questions.solution: Cotton is grown during the summer (monsoon) season, hence it is a Kharif crop.

marking_points.point: Needs warm/summer season and monsoon rain; sown with monsoon in summer

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Based on the ownership, what type of industry is Visakhapatnam Steel Plant?
questions.solution: Public sector industry (owned by Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd.).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: What is meant by cooperative sector industry?
questions.solution: Industries owned and operated by a collective of individuals (producers/workers).

marking_points.point: Owned and operated jointly by a group of individuals

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain the following term: Sericulture
questions.solution: The process of cultivating (rearing) silkworms and extracting silk from them.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain the following term: Integrated steel plant
questions.solution: A steel plant in which all the processes involved in steel making are done in one place.

marking_points.point: All processes of steel making at one location

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain: Mini-steel plants help in conservation of coal.
questions.solution: Mini steel plants use electric furnaces, thereby saving coking coal.

marking_points.point: Use electric furnaces instead of coking coal

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain: Location of sugar industry is shifting to the Southern part of India.
questions.solution: Cooler climate, success of the cooperative movement and higher sucrose content of sugarcane in the South (any one).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give one reason to explain: The electronic industry is growing at a fast rate.
questions.solution: Increasing demand for electronic goods.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: State two conditions that favour the location of cotton textile industry in Ahmedabad.
questions.solution: Regular supply of / proximity to raw material; humid climate; good road and rail network and sea routes; nearby ports for import/export; cheap skilled labour; availability of capital (Mumbai and Ahmedabad are financial centres). (Any two)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: State any one advantage of locating Iron and Steel industry at Rourkela.
questions.solution: Close to raw materials like iron ore.

marking_points.point: Proximity to iron ore (or other valid advantage)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is road transport an important means of transport in India? (Any two reasons)
questions.solution: Ideal for short distances and reaches every village; cost effective; transports people and goods quickly; door-to-door service; roads can be built on hilly terrain where railways/air are not possible. (Any two)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason for each of the following: Northern plain is best suited for the development of Railways.
questions.solution: The Northern Plains have flat terrain and fertile alluvial soil that facilitate construction of straight railway tracks and strong foundations.

marking_points.point: Flat terrain / level land allows easy track construction

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a reason for each of the following: Railways are managed completely by the Central Government.
questions.solution: Railways need huge investment in buying costly coaches, laying tracks etc., hence are managed by the Central Government.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.topic: Inland water transport pros and cons
questions.question: Mention two advantages and one disadvantage of Inland water transport.
questions.solution: Advantages: cheapest means of transport; suitable for carrying bulky materials (also fuel efficient/eco-friendly). Disadvantage: South Indian rivers are non-perennial, so inland waterways cannot be used in dry seasons.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why has airway become more popular than other means of transport? (Any three reasons)
questions.solution: Air transport is the fastest and most comfortable mode; it can reach remote and inaccessible areas like mountains, forests and deserts; it is very useful in war and natural calamities like floods, earthquakes, famines and epidemics.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to the picture below, answer the questions that follow: Which waste management method is depicted here?
questions.solution: Segregation.
questions.figure_desc: Picture showing waste segregation (separate bins for biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste) not reproduced

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: With reference to the picture of the waste management method (segregation): State one way in which this method may be implemented at our home.
questions.solution: Segregating waste into biodegradable and non-biodegradable items (separate bins).

marking_points.point: Separate biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste at home

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain how waste accumulation can be harmful. (Any two points)
questions.solution: Air pollution (acid rain, airborne diseases, bad odour, release of greenhouse gases, chemicals leaking into underground water); water pollution affects human health, land and aquatic animals (eutrophication, biomagnification).

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain how waste generated in the household sector may be made useful. (Give one example)
questions.solution: Glass, metal, plastics, cloth, paper etc. can be reused, e.g. cloth bags made from old clothes instead of plastic bags; donating old clothes, toys and furniture.

marking_points.point: Explains reuse of household waste with an example

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain how waste generated in the industry sector may be made useful. (Give one example)
questions.solution: Some industrial solid wastes can be used directly, e.g. fly ash from power plants is used as a substitute for cement, for making roads and filling low-lying areas.

marking_points.point: Explains use of industrial waste with an example (e.g. fly ash)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Explain how waste generated in the agriculture sector may be made useful. (Give one example)
questions.solution: Dry straw from agriculture can be used to feed cattle (also composting/manure).

marking_points.point: Explains use of agricultural waste with an example

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give two uses of composting.
questions.solution: Compost is a nutrient-rich fertilizer that reduces use of synthetic fertilizers; decreases erosion and improves soil structure; prevents plant diseases and spread of pathogens; microorganisms aerate the soil and convert nitrogen to usable form. (Any two)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why are landfills set up far away from the city? (Any two reasons)
questions.solution: To avoid overflow of waste/water into the city and to keep the city free of waste (also odour, pollution and disease risk). (Any two)
